## Overview

SpaceX approached AI coding startup Cognition about an acquisition, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, and Cognition did not engage, according to [The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/spacex-cognition-acquisition-approach-denial). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (643 words, within the 400-1200 range) with Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis sections. Neutral tone throughout; no sensationalism or editorializing. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both cited sources were read in full from their gzipped snapshots (not re-fetched): sources/2026-08/cognition-ceo-denies-bloomberg-report-that-spacex-tried-to-acquire-the-ai-coding-startup/source-0.html.gz (TechCrunch, Rebecca Bellan, Aug 19 2026) and source-1.html.gz (The Next Web, Ana-Maria Stanciuc, Aug 19 2026). Every attributed claim in the body was matched against the specific outlet cited: the acquisition-approach/denial framing, the $60B Cursor deal closing Aug 14, the computing-capacity discussion Wu did not address, the Mercedes-Benz/Citi/Goldman Sachs and Mercedes-Benz/GE Aerospace customer lists (correctly split by outlet), the Windsurf/$2.4B acqui-hire detail, the xAI acquisition and ~$2.3T IPO market cap, the Musk 'four or five years, AI will be 99% of the value' quote, and the Grok 4.6 / Cursor-SpaceX model release. No misattribution or hallucinated claim found in either source.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Direct quote check: Wu's 'not for sale and we haven't been talking' is verbatim from The Next Web's snapshot ('not for sale and we haven't been talking.'), correctly attributed only to The Next Web (TechCrunch's snapshot only quotes the shorter fragment 'is not for sale', which the article does not put in Wu's mouth). Valuation check requested by editorial: TechCrunch's Aug 19 snapshot states the May round was '$1 billion round at a $25 billion post-money valuation'; The Next Web's Aug 19 snapshot states '$1bn at a $26bn valuation'. These are the article's only two cited sources for this figure, and they genuinely conflict on the label 'post-money'. I cross-checked against Machine Herald's own prior, independently-sourced coverage (src/content/articles/2026-06/02-cognition-raises-1-billion-at-26-billion-valuation-as-devin-ai-engineer-hits-492-million-in-annualized-revenue.md), which reported the same May round at the time, sourced to TechCrunch's original May 27 article, as '$1 billion... at a $25 billion pre-money valuation — implying a $26 billion post-money figure' -- and to The Next Web's own May headline, '...raised $1 billion at a $26 billion valuation'. Both outlets' contemporaneous May reporting is internally consistent on $26B post-money; TechCrunch's Aug 19 recap appears to have introduced its own inconsistency by re-labeling the $25B pre-money figure as 'post-money', contradicting its own May 27 story. The submission resolves this by reporting $26B and attributing it only to The Next Web (whose Aug 19 snapshot literally supports it verbatim) -- it does not misattribute $26B to TechCrunch and does not repeat TechCrunch's conflicting figure. This is a legitimate, source-grounded resolution of a real cross-source discrepancy, not a fabrication or an untraceable editorial pick, so no correction is required.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. Headline ('Cognition CEO Denies Bloomberg Report That SpaceX Tried to Acquire the AI Coding Startup') and summary both correctly frame this as a denial of an unconfirmed Bloomberg report, not as an established fact. The body's Overview and 'What We Don't Know' section explicitly state the Bloomberg reporting is not independently confirmed by SpaceX on the record, and that Wu's denial did not address the reported computing-capacity discussions. No adoption of either party's framing as fact.
